Question:
Title: You are nature 🌍💚

Body:

We know you care about the planet, and guess what? You’re a part of it.

This short journey is about your connection with nature, how it makes you feel, and how you show up for it.

By joining in, you’re helping us build something new — a way to show just how much a young person's connection to nature matters.

Ready? Let’s explore 🌱✨
Do you feel connected to nature or natural places?
Answer Options:
•       🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿 = Very connected (Got to row 4)
        •       🌿🌿🌿🌿 = Connected  (Got to row 4)
        •       🌿🌿🌿 = Somewhate connected  (Got to row 4)
        •       🌿🌿 = A little connected  (Got to row 4)
        •       🌿 = Not connected (Got to row 6)
Hypothesis Alignment: Directly supports the hypothesis around 'stronger connection to nature'. Relevant to the objective of measuring internal shifts.
Insight Clarity: Measures perceived connection to nature — a key emotional/psychological indicator of environmental affinity.
Indicators & Value: Useful for program-level reporting, storytelling about transformation, and policy arguments about the benefits of nature connection.
Comment: These two questions explore different aspects of nature connection: one focuses on a deeper emotional or spiritual bond with natural places, while the other emphasizes a sensory, embodied experience of being in nature. Keeping both captures complementary dimensions—identity-based vs. experiential—which support different insights for program design, storytelling, and evaluation.

Question: “Where do you usually feel connected to nature?”
Answer Options:
•        In parks, beaches, or green spaces
        •        In the countryside, by rivers, or in wild areas
        •        Hiking, camping, or outdoor adventures
        •        In gardens or farms
        •        At school (playing or doing nature activities)
        •        Outside where I live or study (yard, street, school grounds)
        •        Playing sports outdoors
        •        Walking or commuting through nature
        •        Watching nature shows or reading about nature
        •        Other (tell us!): ____________
Hypothesis Alignment: Supports understanding of the context for nature connection, which may shape program design or site-based interventions.
Insight Clarity: Identifies types of environments that foster connection — urban green spaces, coastal areas, etc.
Indicators & Value: Location clustering insights, thematic preferences; informs Fellows’ design strategies and storytelling of diverse nature experiences.

Question: How often do you do things in nature that you enjoy?
Answer Options:
•        Never – I don’t spend time in nature
        •        Rarely – A few times a year
        •        Sometimes – About once a month
        •        Often – A few times a month
        •        Very often – Every week or more
Hypothesis Alignment: Supports nature connection via behavior tracking. Relevant to measuring sustained engagement with natural settings.
Insight Clarity: Reveals time spent in nature, which may correlate with wellbeing and connection. Tracks behavior rather than sentiment.
Indicators & Value: Distribution of responses by category; trend shifts over time or by program. Valuable for monitoring actual behavior change.

Question:
Please indicate if you agree or disagree with each statement below.
(Options: Disagree / Neutral / Agree)
Answer Options:
•        I feel comfortable in nature.
        •        I am curious about how nature works.
        •        I can interact with nature confidently. 
        •        I can tell if the surrounding nature is healthy. 
        •        I have a strong attachment to natural places.
        •        My experiences in nature help shape my identity.
        •        I feel upset when the surrounding nature is unhealthy. 
        •        I actively take care of nature.
        •        I take a leadership role in caring for nature. 
        •        I feel responsible for protecting nature for future generations.
        •        I have a deep sense of unity with nature.
        •        I don’t easily feel bored in nature. I feel bored in nature
Hypothesis Alignment: Aligns with ‘comfort in nature’ as a proxy for connection and wellbeing. Supports internal shift measurement.
Insight Clarity: Gauges self-reported comfort in various natural conditions — part of psychological ease and resilience.
Indicators & Value: shifts over time, comparisons by region/program. Useful in demonstrating climate confidence and nature readiness.

Hypothesis Alignment: Explores how nature shapes personal values and decision-making, reflecting internal shift in identity.
Insight Clarity: Reveals depth of nature’s integration into youth worldview and agency.
Indicators & Value: narrative evidence for purpose-driven learning or curriculum design.

Indicators & Value: reporting frequent action; useful in showing nature-driven behavior change in policy and storytelling contexts.
